rules.statement: A host with an app serves only credentials that declare that app: another one, or none, is Rejected(APP_MISMATCH) (SCP-11); without a host app the credential's app applies. On a gateway the host app of a route's requests is the route's metadata cosec-app-id, ahead of cosec.authorization.scope.app-id; a cosec-app-id that is not a string (a number, a boolean, a list or a map is not read as its text) or cannot be an app id (SCP-10) fails the request as an unmodelled error (500), never leaves it without a host app.

rules.statement: CoSec-Space-Id and CoSec-Device-Id are read from headers only, never from the query string. When the values of one of them differ, the request cannot be read unambiguously and is answered 400. A blank value beside a non-blank one differs too; only values that are all blank read as not sent, and blank is ASCII whitespace only, so a value of Unicode spaces is a value.

rules.statement: A declared app that cannot be an app id (blank, *, containing ':' or a control character, or longer than 128 characters: the rule of a tenant id) is Rejected(APP_MISMATCH), with or without a host app. An app document's key (SnapshotKey.App) takes only such an id, so the control plane takes no app the data plane could never read: analyze refuses one with 400, and a candidate document with a binding in such an app, wherever it is, is a V2 finding (400) at the binding's app, so a document that holds one must remove it in its next change, and a change that only removes it is valid. The control plane skips such an app wherever it would build a key from a document (back-references, their repair, the checks, the grant analysis), and a stored record that names one (an open change of such an app, an instance status entry, an app list entry, a back-reference set's member) is skipped alone, never stopping maintenance or a write; the control API answers such a change 409.
The app is checked before the space: a request failing both is Rejected(APP_MISMATCH).
guards: model:ScopeResolverTest#the app is checked before the space

rules.statement: A space id beginning with ( is reserved for CoSec: a declared one is Rejected(SPACE_NOT_MEMBER) whatever the principal claims, a document binding in one does not compile, and the control plane writes the default space as (default).

rules.source: RFC 0004 §4.6 (round-1 review, 2026-10-26; RC1-15), split from SCP-7 by batch R4 (2026-11-08)
rules.statement: An app a credential declares that cannot be an app id (blank, *, containing ':' or a control character, or longer than 128 characters: the rule of a tenant id) is Rejected(APP_MISMATCH), with or without a host app. An app document's key (SnapshotKey.App) takes only such an id, so the control plane takes no app the data plane could never read: analyze refuses one with 400, and a candidate document with a binding in such an app, wherever it is, is a V2 finding (400) at the binding's app. A stored record that names such an app (a change of one, or a head it was checked with; an instance status entry; a back-reference set's member; an app list entry; a head holding a binding in one) is a format error, and whatever reads it fails closed: nothing skips the record. Reading such a change is 503, a publish or a repair over such a head or set fails without moving the head, a maintenance pass stops without reclaiming, and the grant analysis takes every app as unknown.

rules.statement: Tokens and API keys declare the app they belong to (aud, one value). A host with an app serves only credentials declaring that app: another one, or none, is Rejected(APP_MISMATCH). Without a host app the credential's app applies, and a credential declaring none is in no app and reads no app document. An anonymous request has no credential, so its app is the host's. A forwarded gateway identity is the credential behind a gateway and is checked the same way. A request cannot declare an app: CoSec-App-Id is not read. A token whose aud is not one string that can be an app id is invalid, on every path that verifies one.

rules.statement: The app of a token is its issuer's decision. A tenant switch issues the new token for the app its TenantSwitch answers (TenantMembership.app), which must be one a token can carry as its aud, and otherwise for the previous token's app. An app the switch's credentials name (targetAppId) reaches the new token only through that answer, never as named.

rules.statement: A tenant id and an app id are each one path segment: neither holds '/' (ScopeResolver.isValidAppId, the rule of both, and SnapshotKey.Tenant and SnapshotKey.App with it). The resources the control plane authorizes on put the id between '/' (doc/tenant/<t>/..., scope/<t>/<a>/<s>), where a pattern's one-segment capture and a trailing ** would take a longer id for another tenant's. The principal that would cross is a platform principal: the hard rule (TenantIsolation) lets one act on any tenant, so for it the resource string is the only thing between tenants. A platform principal holding cosec:read on doc/tenant/acme and doc/tenant/acme/** (one tenant, delegated by resource pattern) reads tenant acme's document, and GET /documents/tenant:acme%2Fwest is 400 for it: no key names that tenant. ControlResources refuses '/' in a segment as a second line, so either line alone keeps the tenants apart. A token of such a tenant or app is an invalid credential (401 token-invalid, alike on every adapter); a forwarded identity of such a tenant is 400 invalid-request; a principal an authenticator answers in one is unresolved (503); a credential's declared app of one is Rejected(APP_MISMATCH). A stored record under such an id is an SCP-10 format error of the whole record, whose failure names the record and the id. cosec-migrate refuses such a tenant or app id at the id (SLASH_IN_ID), and an API key of such a tenant, and writes nothing.
